close_reason: Made RuntimeDemand formulas read-only over explicit settled semantic inputs; proved schedule-independent final inputs, outputs, and exact product requests across independent, self-recursive, and mutual-cycle fixtures; added canonical subprocess and mutation gates.
description:
## Goal

Make the eventual per-executable `RuntimeDemand(E)` formula required by
fz-kdt.4 a read-only function of authoritative facts and current demand inputs.

The reactive scheduler may evaluate only changed formulas and may evaluate
independent or cyclic formulas in any order. A demand formula therefore cannot
require a peer formula to run first or use mutation of the shared type arena as
an ordering channel.

## Verified current state

At a3a9761d1, `settle_demand_cone` uses a Jacobi ascent whose semantic demand
values are documented as order-invariant. It nevertheless sorts cone members by
`StableSortKey` because member derivation mints `Ty` values into the shared
`Types` arena.

The same issue exists inside one member:

- callable producers are sorted by `ValueId` before callable-flow derivation;
- callable-flow maps are sorted before boundary-demand contribution derivation;
- callable surfaces are canonically sorted before activation keys and callable
  surfaces are interned;
- `own_surface`, callable-clause projection, `CallableSurface::new`, and
  `World::activation_key` can intern types while demand is being derived.

Those sorts are valid current determinism barriers, but a per-executable
reactive formula cannot depend on a global peer order.

No production test currently evaluates the same independent or cyclic demand
formulas in several explicit orders.

## Evidence boundary

Do not use the existing cross-process `CallableConstruction` cache-hit
divergence as proof of this defect.

A fresh six-process run on
`fixtures2/behavior/fz_f98_range_map_converges.fz` reproduced only the excluded
cache-hit redistribution: 7 of 15 pairs agreed on per-identity cache-hit counts.
All 15 pairs agreed on canonical `RuntimeDemand` settlements and canonical
`CallableConstruction` settlements. The differing cache hits therefore do not
prove that demand formulas settled different values or produced different
product sets.

Likewise, raw arena slot numbers are not a cross-process semantic comparator.
Cross-process comparisons must use the faithful canonical identities already
carried by the public trace. Interner equivalence defects remain owned by
fz-kdt.48.

If the shuffled-formula harness does not reproduce the cache-hit divergence,
route that divergence through the product-work causality investigation rather
than retaining an unsupported attribution here.

## Output contract

- Deriving `RuntimeDemand(E)`, its callable-flow facts, and its target
  contributions reads authoritative facts and current demand inputs only.
- Formula evaluation does not intern types, allocate address variables, or
  create activation identities in the shared `World`.
- Every type-bearing identity required by the formula is constructed at the
  earliest authoritative phase or represented by canonical structural data
  supplied as an input.
- Independent and cyclic formulas publish semantically identical values,
  contributions, and requested product identities under every tested order.
- The implementation needs no global formula-order sort, raw-id translation
  table, or demand-local cache.
- Canonical member ordering that is part of callable-wrapper semantics remains;
  only ordering used to serialize formula-side interner mutation is removed.

## Strategy

1. Add a focused harness around the member-level demand derivation boundary.
   Evaluate the same independent pair, self-cycle, and mutual cycle in forward,
   reverse, and seeded orders.
2. Record the complete inputs, canonical demand answer, callable-flow answer,
   target contributions, and requested product keys for every member.
3. Add a type-arena mutation tripwire around one formula evaluation.
4. Trace every mutation reached from demand derivation, including address
   construction, callable-clause projection, own-surface derivation, callable
   surface construction, and activation-key creation.
5. Move each construction to the authoritative fact that first knows it, reuse
   an already canonical identity, or carry canonical structural data into the
   formula.
6. Remove the cone-member `StableSortKey` barrier and the demand-local ordering
   whose sole purpose was stabilizing interner side effects.
7. Re-run the shuffled harness and production determinism checks with no
   schedule-dependent translation or caching layer.

## TDD and acceptance

- One formula evaluation leaves the type arena and address-variable inventory
  unchanged.
- Forward, reverse, and at least two seeded orders over independent formulas
  yield identical canonical demand values, callable-flow facts, contributions,
  and requested product multisets.
- The same assertion holds for self recursion and a two-member mutual cycle.
- Removing the global cone-member sort does not move semantic answers, canonical
  product identities, or backend programs.
- `00420_enum_take_drop_split`, `enum_predicate_search`, and
  `fz_f98_range_map_converges` produce byte-identical canonical backend dumps
  across shuffled formula orders and separate processes.
- Existing callable-wrapper order stress and construction-member canonical-order
  gates remain green.
- No new global sort, stable-id translation table, shadow cache, or
  schedule-dependent memo is introduced.

Persistent same-root no-op evaluation belongs to fz-kdt.4 once demand is an
ordinary retained fact; it is not acceptance for this prerequisite.

## Checks and documentation

Run the focused shuffle and arena-mutation tests, demand-cone tests while the
cone still exists, callable-wrapper stress, cross-process causal comparison,
backend determinism, the three target fixtures through interp/run/build, the
full library and single-threaded fixture matrix, and clippy with warnings
denied.

Update demand/fact-engine documentation to describe formulas as read-only over
canonical authoritative inputs. Remove claims that correctness requires a
stable global formula order or cross-process equality of raw arena slots.
title: Make RuntimeDemand derivation read-only and prove per-executable order independence
